items.stem: What does enabling WAL (write-ahead logging) mode in SQLite primarily improve?

options.text: Readers can continue reading while a writer is appending, improving read-write concurrency
options.rationale: Correct: WAL lets readers see a consistent snapshot while a single writer appends changes.

options.text: It allows many simultaneous writers to the same database
options.rationale: SQLite still permits only one writer at a time, even in WAL mode.

options.text: It removes the need for indexes
options.rationale: WAL is about journaling and concurrency, not query planning.

items.explanation: Correct: WAL lets readers see a consistent snapshot while a single writer appends changes.

items.stem: Which statements about SQLite are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Foreign key enforcement must be turned on per connection with a pragma
options.rationale: Correct: foreign keys are off by default and enabled with PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON.

options.text: SQLite stores the whole database in a single file
options.rationale: Correct: a SQLite database is a single cross-platform file.

options.text: SQLite requires a separate server process to run
options.rationale: SQLite is embedded and serverless; it runs in-process.

options.text: Column types are strictly enforced like in most client-server databases
options.rationale: SQLite uses flexible type affinity rather than strict typing.

items.explanation: Correct: foreign keys are off by default and enabled with PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON.; Correct: a SQLite database is a single cross-platform file.

items.stem: A frequent lookup by email is slow on a large table. What is the most direct fix?

options.text: Create an index on the email column so the planner can avoid a full table scan
options.rationale: Correct: an index lets the query planner locate matching rows without scanning every row.

options.text: Rewrite the query to SELECT * instead of listing columns
options.rationale: Selecting more columns does not speed up the lookup.
Transactions are unrelated to lookup speed here.

options.text: Switch the column to JSON storage
options.rationale: JSON storage would not accelerate an equality lookup.

items.explanation: Correct: an index lets the query planner locate matching rows without scanning every row.
